name: The 2022 Self-Audit
claim: It wasn't Twitter — it's the parties. Re-running OnScript's own 2022 predecessor finding on official congressional press releases (not tweets), with matched member counts and co-signed statements removed: Democrats' independent week-to-week language overlap is ~85% higher than Republicans', in 71% of weeks. The tighter-coordination signal is structural, not a platform artifact.

numbers.metric: mean pairwise weekly content-5-gram Jaccard overlap, matched member counts (min per party per week, cap 40)

confounds_tested: member-count asymmetry -> controlled: parties subsampled to equal N each week

joint/co-signed releases -> controlled: verbatim cross-member releases excluded; gap WIDENED (D 0.00173->0.00176, R 0.00102->0.00095); R co-signs MORE (48 vs 37 dropped), so co-signing works against the finding
coverage -> both parties measured in the same weeks, scale-free per-pair Jaccard
split_result: n/a (pre-registered as a targeted replication of the 2021-2022 window); internal robustness = 71% of weeks agree
chart_spec: paired weekly overlap, D vs R, 105 weeks of 2021-2022; or the two mean bars with the 71%-of-weeks annotation
receipts_note: receipts = specific high-peak D phrases in 117 from the phrase index (e.g. a phrase said by 30+ D members in one week, expandable to member+date+url); pull at publish time
graveyard_context: shipped alongside the Wave-S1 graveyard: this CONFIRMED sits next to 4 REFUTED + 2 ARTIFACT — the discipline that rejected the artifacts is what makes this replication trustworthy
drip_slot: flagship — the integrity-flex opener for the Search program
